{"author":{"id":"U_kgDOD9HSnA","is_bot":false,"login":"jeffwall-curlewlabs","name":"Jeffrey Wall"},"body":"### Describe the bug

`gh run view --log` (and `--log-failed`) silently drops everything after a log line longer than 64 KiB, up to the end of the log segment being printed. That is the rest of the step when gh can split the job's log into steps, or the rest of the job when it prints the job as one `UNKNOWN STEP` segment. There is no warning and the command exits 0, so the output looks complete when it isn't.

The cause is `copyLogWithLinePrefix` in `pkg/cmd/run/view/view.go`:

```go
func copyLogWithLinePrefix(w io.Writer, r io.Reader, prefix string) error {
	sanitized := transform.NewReader(r, &asciisanitizer.Sanitizer{})
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(sanitized)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s%s\n", prefix, scanner.Text())
	}
	return nil
}
```

`bufio.NewScanner` has a default max token size of 64 KiB (`bufio.MaxScanTokenSize`). When a line exceeds it, `Scan()` returns false with `bufio.ErrTooLong`, and `scanner.Err()` is never checked, so the loop ends early for that segment and the function returns nil. `displayLogSegments` then moves on to the next segment, which is why the loss is per step.

Lines this long are common in real job logs: tools that print JSON event streams (for example, AI code-review CLIs emitting one JSON object per line) or build tools dumping a large status line.

### Affected version

```
gh version 2.102.1 (2026-10-20)
```

The function is unchanged on `trunk` as of v2.103.3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I haven't run this minimal workflow; it is the smallest case the code above implies. The measurements further down come from real runs.

1. Run a workflow with a step that prints a line longer than 64 KiB followed by a marker, e.g.:

   ```yaml
   - run: |
       python3 -c "print('x' * 70000)"
       echo "AFTER-LONG-LINE"
   ```

2. `gh run view <run-id> --log | grep -c AFTER-LONG-LINE` prints `0`.
3. `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/jobs/<job-id>/logs | grep -c AFTER-LONG-LINE` prints `1`.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: the whole log is printed, or, failing that, gh reports an error instead of exiting 0 with partial output.

Actual: the segment's output silently ends at the line before the over-long one, and the next step's output follows as if nothing were missing.

What I measured, on a private repository's runs: across six completed runs of one workflow, `gh run view --attempt 1 --log` was missing part of a job's log in five, while the run's log archive (`/actions/runs/<id>/attempts/1/logs`) had all of it. The one complete run was the only one with no line over 64 KiB. Across the six, the longest line gh printed was about 51,000 characters, and wherever I traced a cut, the dropped text began right at a line over 64 KiB. In a job from a different workflow, gh printed 2,932 of the job's 13,718 lines: one step was cut right before a line of about 139,000 characters, and thousands of lines of that step were never printed.

A possible fix: read with `bufio.Reader.ReadString('\n')` (no line-length limit), or give the scanner a buffer larger than any realistic log line (`scanner.Buffer(...)`). Checking `scanner.Err()` alone would surface the problem but still drop the rest of the segment.

### Logs

N/A. The command exits 0 and logs nothing about the truncation.
